recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-16333 unless a future terminology decision changes extensible-binding semantics or the valueset-reference extension.
issue_request: FHIR-16333 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core vocab clarification for STU3 asking for additional formal guidance on binding strengths. The accepted resolution required valueset-reference extension guidance for extensible bindings when a code falls outside the bound value set, and added that Example binding strength may use well-specified realm-specific value sets.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn commit 7aec658b3689440042c229c74d080b4d6c2520d5, matching Jira's svn revision 14677 comment. That commit changed source/terminologies.html by adding the realm-specific Example binding sentence and initial extensible-binding wording. Follow-up commit cc33213f906a949e5bb7ff4af5db1183810afe4a, for FHIR-17402, moved the valueset-reference rule into an explicit note.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml lists source/terminologies.html as the built Terminology / Using Codes page. Later Published issue FHIR-29968 rewrote extensible-binding usage notes in commit 25395f9580db54e0300d46d1daeeb13852bd5284 while preserving the valueset-reference rule. The valueset-reference StructureDefinition now lives in the FHIR Extension Pack and its comment also states the same extensible-binding rule. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/terminologies.html already says that valueset-reference must point to a different value set definition when an extensibly-bound instance uses a code outside the bound value set, and the Example binding section already permits well-specified realm-specific ValueSets as example bindings in the base specification.
